pairs.subject: concurrent-vcs
pairs.evidence: scripts/case-loops/sources/kiosek-slice.ts:168 The shared gitignored .kiosek-cache/pdfs cache is trusted on bare file existence while line 182 writes each PDF in place with no .part-and-rename, so a truncated or sibling-in-progress file passes the check, is never refetched and fails only at parse time, the exact population failure shared-resource-arbitration names; the other eight techniques are not engaged because these scripts run no git operation.

techniques.evidence: scripts/case-loops/sources/kiosek-slice.ts:168 Population check is existence only, with no size or completeness test, and the writer at line 182 is non-atomic, although lib/ingest/parsedText.ts and dataor.ts use .part-then-rename for the same cache class. The store side is better: kiosek-validate.ts:26 refuses the live path and apply-batch.ts:649 guards live commits, so the deviation is confined to the PDF cache.
scripts/case-loops/apply-batch.ts:53 Here --commit is a graph-store write; no VCS commit or commit hook exists in this context's files.
scripts/case-loops/persist-batch.ts:140 The commit is a DB upsert; these scripts create no VCS commit that could be read back.
scripts/case-loops/persist-batch.ts:2 Fan-in is of data payloads into the store; no branch or worktree is merged here, and a search for worktree found none under scripts/case-loops.
scripts/case-loops/sources/kiosek-build-payload.ts:10 File ownership is assigned in a doc outside this context; these scripts neither read nor write a session ledger.
scripts/case-loops/apply-batch.ts:327 The only mention of git in the ten files, as a passive record; no index handling, and GIT_INDEX_FILE has no hit under scripts/case-loops.
scripts/case-loops/sources/kiosek-build-payload.ts:149 The scripts only write their output files and leave staging to the caller; git stash and git add have no hit under scripts/case-loops.
scripts/case-loops/sources/kiosek-validate.ts:11 The isolation here is a copy of a data store, not a working copy of the repository; no worktree is created or removed.
scripts/case-loops/persist-batch.ts:25 Claim means a factual assertion carrying a citation, not a lease on a code unit; the map's claim and commit tokens are a vocabulary collision.

pairs.registryProposal: shared-resource-arbitration's population check asks that a file exist and be non-empty, which a truncated non-empty partial write still passes; the technique should name the producer-side rule (write to a temporary name, rename last) as the counterpart, since no reader-side size test can detect truncation in a format with no declared length.
